Title: Full recursive source capture
Requirement: The system shall capture the entire source tree recursively and record every encountered file in the backup's index.
Rationale: No source file may be silently dropped, including hidden, system and dot-prefixed files and directories.
AcceptanceCriteria: Every file in a known source tree, including nested, Unicode and bracketed names, appears exactly once in the backup's index.

Title: Deterministic content hashing
Requirement: The system shall produce a deterministic canonical XXH128 content digest, represented as 32 uppercase hexadecimal characters, for each file.
Rationale: The content digest identifies content for change detection and deduplication.
AcceptanceCriteria: Identical bytes produce identical 32-character uppercase hexadecimal digests; the distinct reference inputs produce their distinct expected digests.

Title: Content deduplication
Requirement: The system shall store exactly one physical object per content hash and length, both across runs and within a single run, with every logical name recoverable from that object even when extensions or compressibility differ.
Rationale: Identical content should consume storage once without losing any logical path.
AcceptanceCriteria: Identical source files produce one stored object whether first seen together or in separate runs. Additional entries are marked Duplicate and restore from the same content; differing extensions or compressibility still yield exactly one object.

Title: Selective compression
Requirement: When CompressEnabled is true, the system shall compress newly stored content according to CompressProbe and SR-081: extension exemptions apply in off and excluded-extensions modes and below the 256 KiB floor; above that floor in always mode the measured result governs regardless of filename. Stored form, the index's Compressed value and the stored extension shall agree. CompressEnabled=false shall disable both probing and compression. FILEBACKUP_7Z_LEVEL shall select compression effort from digits 0–9, defaulting to 9 when absent or empty; invalid values shall be refused for a compression-enabled Backup action under SR-037, while other actions remain usable. Compression level shall not change the compression decision or restore compatibility.
Rationale: Stored naming and index metadata must agree with the stored form so content can be located and restored reliably.
AcceptanceCriteria: Compressible content is stored compressed and marked accordingly; exempt content remains raw where the configured mode honors exemptions. Above the floor under always, compressible content with an exempt extension is compressed and incompressible content with a normally compressible extension remains raw. Compression effort 1 and the default effort 9 preserve the same storage decision and remain restorable.

Title: Dated point-in-time snapshot
Requirement: When a run changes the backup's indexed state relative to the prior completed backup, the system shall expose a complete snapshot identified by that prior backup's completion date. Changes include added, removed, content-changed or metadata-changed entries, duplicate-content additions and removals whose bytes remain shared. No snapshot shall be created for an index-identical run or the latest live state.
Rationale: Only superseded states need historical snapshots; a logical change supersedes a state even when it writes no new physical content. Complete publication protects recovery after interruption.
AcceptanceCriteria: A changed run produces a complete snapshot with its own index, including duplicate-only additions and shared-content removals. A no-op run adds none. Same-second completion dates are disambiguated, and no visible snapshot lacks its complete index.

Title: Preserve shared content during removal
Requirement: When a source file is removed, the system shall retain its stored content while any entry of the final live index still references it, and preserve content needed for historical recovery.
Rationale: Removing one duplicate must not delete content another still references.
AcceptanceCriteria: Removing one of two identical files retains their shared content in the live backup; removing the last live reference preserves it in historical storage.

Title: Self-contained restore kit
Requirement: Each run shall provide a self-contained restore kit in the backup root and each dated snapshot, independent of the backup engine. A snapshot shall retain its original kit unless explicitly refreshed with Verify -RefreshKits. Older kit launchers shall remain recognized as infrastructure. The kit shall support Windows and macOS launchers, POSIX restore portability, and writable restored files.
Rationale: Recovery must need only the backup folder and the declared commonly available restore tools, not the backup application.
AcceptanceCriteria: The live backup and each snapshot contain a complete usable kit; restoration needs no backup-engine code. Compatible older stores remain restorable and retained older launcher artifacts are treated as infrastructure.

Title: Bit-exact restore from backup alone
Requirement: The restore capability shall rebuild the source tree byte-for-byte from the backup folder's contents, expanding compressed content and recovering entries with no stored location from other available copies, without the repository or a restore-time package installation.
Rationale: Realizes SN-005; this is the core promise of the tool.
AcceptanceCriteria: Restoring a backup (incl. compressed and hash-fallback rows) on a clean environment reproduces every original file with identical bytes.

Title: Reject restore target inside backup
Requirement: The restorer shall refuse a target physically inside the backup folder, resolving junctions and symbolic links when determining containment. It shall refuse any indexed destination that escapes the restore target root, count that entry unrestored and fail loudly.
Rationale: Writing into the backup can corrupt its stored content, and a traversal entry must not write outside the chosen target.
AcceptanceCriteria: Pointing the restore at a path within the backup folder is rejected with a clear error and no files written; a manifest row whose RelativePath escapes the target root is refused, counted unrestored, and the run fails loudly per SR-029. A target beneath a junction that resolves into the backup root is refused; a genuinely external target, a prefix-sharing sibling, and a nested target all keep their existing outcomes.

Title: Point-in-time restore from a dated snapshot
Requirement: Restoring a dated snapshot shall reproduce that snapshot's indexed state byte-for-byte, using shared content available across the backup root and snapshots without overlaying any newer state.
Rationale: Selecting an earlier date must recover that date's content, not newer versions.
AcceptanceCriteria: Restoring the snapshot for backup N reproduces every file as of N, including old bytes of modified files; restoring the live root reproduces the latest state, byte-exact.

Title: Deterministic rehash scheduling
Requirement: The system shall determine whether unchanged content is due for rehashing from HashRecalcFreq values A/E/D/W/M/Y/N, the reference time and persisted last-hash-run time.
Rationale: Scheduling must consistently trade repeated content checks against backup runtime.
AcceptanceCriteria: For a fixed reference time and persisted last run, A/E always rehash, N never rehashes, and D/W/M/Y rehash at the documented boundary crossings.

Title: StoredAsHashSize is the constant 'Hash'
Requirement: Every written index entry shall carry StoredAsHashSize='Hash'; 'Original' shall never be written and shall identify a legacy format refused under SR-061.
Rationale: The column remains part of the nine-column external index contract even though only one storage layout is supported.
AcceptanceCriteria: New, adopted and evicted index entries all carry StoredAsHashSize='Hash'; none is written with 'Original'.

Title: Independent multi-set processing
Requirement: The system shall process each BackupSet independently such that one set's failure does not abort the others, and the overall exit code shall be non-zero if any set failed.
Rationale: Realizes SN-009 and SN-011; a multi-set scheduled job must be resilient and honest about partial failure.
AcceptanceCriteria: Given multiple sets where one fails, the others still complete and the process exits non-zero.

Title: Optional non-fatal mail
Requirement: The system shall send a success/failure email only when SMTP is fully configured and -NoMail is not set, and shall treat any mail failure as a logged warning that never changes the backup's success status.
Rationale: Notification is optional and must not change the backup's actual success or failure.
AcceptanceCriteria: With SMTP omitted or -NoMail, no mail is sent and the run proceeds; a send failure is logged WARN and does not flip exit code.

Title: Non-interactive automation safety
Requirement: The system shall provide -NonInteractive operation that never blocks on a prompt and reports errors with non-zero status. A restore missing its target under -NonInteractive, redirected input, or a session with neither console nor desktop shall print usage and exit 2. The POSIX restore interface shall require --target-root unless interactive selection is explicitly requested.
Rationale: Realizes SN-011; a hanging scheduled task is a silent backup failure.
AcceptanceCriteria: Non-interactive dependency resolution never prompts; missing optional media tools degrade to absent and fatal conditions return non-zero. A missing restore target with no console or desktop yields usage and exit 2.

Title: Stale staging guard
Requirement: The system shall refuse unfinished staging that holds content, a prune ownership record, a live or unproven owner, a symbolic link or reparse point, or unreadable evidence. Hidden, system and dot-named content counts. An incomplete index-publication artifact is not unique content and shall not alone prevent recovery. Staging proved empty and stale, or holding only a stale backup owner record confirmed unchanged, shall be recovered without risking unique content. Recovery shall preserve unexpected content and retain abandoned staging when safe cleanup fails. A refusal shall name the staging area, publish no snapshot and leave the stored tree unchanged. Other staging creation failures shall retain their actual cause rather than be misreported as existing staging.
Rationale: Mixing unfinished work from different runs can destroy the only copy of historical content. Safe evidence-based recovery avoids permanently blocking scheduled backups after a dead run, while uncertainty must favor preservation.
AcceptanceCriteria: Content-bearing, prune-held, unreadable, linked, fresh or changing staging is refused without moving or deleting it or altering stored state. Empty stale staging or backup-marker-only staging older than the declared threshold, with a reader floor of 1800 seconds and an unchanged confirmation sample after the SR-075 wait, is recovered and the run completes. Unexpected content or cleanup failure preserves the abandoned area and reports recovery guidance.

Title: Missing config fails clearly
Requirement: The system shall throw a clear error and exit non-zero when the configured config file does not exist, performing no destructive action.
Rationale: Realizes SN-014.
AcceptanceCriteria: Invoking with a non-existent ConfigPath throws "config not found" and exits non-zero; nothing is written to any target.

Title: Required-dependency enforcement
Requirement: Before hashing, the system shall ensure the required XXH128 capability is available and shall fail with remediation guidance when the runtime or dependency is unsupported.
Rationale: Content identification must not silently proceed with a missing or incorrect hashing capability.
AcceptanceCriteria: An available bundled hashing dependency is used; otherwise dependency initialization succeeds or fails with remediation guidance, including in non-interactive mode. Runtime versions below the supported PowerShell 7 floor are rejected.

Title: External-tool enforcement and degradation
Requirement: The system shall fail before backup processing if compression is selected but the compression tool cannot be resolved; unavailable optional media measurement shall be skipped.
Rationale: Realizes SN-016; the manifest must never claim raw bytes are compressed.
AcceptanceCriteria: A compression-enabled run without its required compression tool exits non-zero before processing any set; unavailable media measurement leaves MediaMBPerSec blank.

Title: Literal path safety
Requirement: File operations shall preserve Unicode, bracketed, parenthesized and space-containing names literally, without wildcard expansion.
Rationale: Path syntax must not reinterpret a legitimate source name or prevent faithful recovery.
AcceptanceCriteria: A source tree containing Unicode and [bracketed]/(paren) names backs up and restores with names intact.

Title: Root-only infrastructure filtering
Requirement: The system shall classify backup infrastructure only at the backup root and shall preserve identically named nested user files as data.
Rationale: Nested names that resemble infrastructure are still user content.
AcceptanceCriteria: A nested file named like the backup index is backed up and restored as data; true root-level restore-kit infrastructure is excluded from source data.

Title: Restore capacity check
Requirement: The restorer shall check sufficient free space at the target, accounting for expanded content size, and report insufficient capacity before producing a partial tree.
Rationale: A target that cannot hold the restored content must be identified before partial recovery.
AcceptanceCriteria: A target without enough room is rejected with a capacity error based on decompressed sizes.

Title: Idempotent deterministic re-run
Requirement: An identical run with no source changes shall produce identical index entries and no spurious change content.
Rationale: Deterministic unchanged runs avoid needless history and storage churn.
AcceptanceCriteria: Two consecutive no-change runs yield byte-identical index entries and an empty change set.

Title: Manifest schema round-trip
Requirement: The nine-column index contract (DataPath, RelativePath, Length, LastWriteTimeStr, xxH2Hash, Compressed, StoredAsHashSize, Duplicate, MediaMBPerSec) shall preserve length and modification-time values on roundtrip, accept null or empty record sets, and be published atomically under SR-082.
Rationale: The index is the shared contract for capturing and restoring files.
AcceptanceCriteria: Written and reread entries preserve numeric lengths and date values; null and empty sets are accepted; a missing index yields an empty record set.

Title: Cross-change duplicate collapse
Requirement: After a run the system shall retain shared historical content once across snapshots while keeping each historical state restorable.
Rationale: Realizes SN-002 within SN-004 history; keeps change history space-efficient.
AcceptanceCriteria: Identical prior-version content across change folders is stored once and still restorable from each referencing change folder.

Title: Dated historical storage
Requirement: Each snapshot shall retain the complete point-in-time index and only the content superseded at the next run; unchanged content shall remain recoverable from the shared pool. Current backup and restore operations shall support only the dated-snapshot format.
Rationale: Sharing unchanged content keeps history space-efficient. Older historical formats remain recoverable through their own bundled kits.
AcceptanceCriteria: A snapshot stores superseded data, recovers unchanged content from the pool, and current operations do not read or write the retired historical format.

Title: First-run setup and discoverable docs
Requirement: The system shall provide a configuration builder and discoverable quick-start documentation enabling a new user to configure and complete a first backup, with required dependencies installed on first use.
Rationale: Realizes SN-012; onboarding must not require reverse-engineering the config schema.
AcceptanceCriteria: Following the quick-start and using the configuration builder produces a valid configuration and successful first backup; the required hashing dependency installs on first use.

Title: Restore fails loudly on unrecoverable content
Requirement: The restorer shall restore every recoverable index entry, log each unrestored entry and its cause, and report a terminating error with the unrestored count and non-zero status for scripted callers. Missing content, failed recovery, failed extraction and unhealed ContentMismatch shall count as failures. Complete recovery shall report exit 0.
Rationale: Silent partial recovery defeats the backup's purpose; automation must be able to rely on the exit status.
AcceptanceCriteria: Deleting a restored row's only data source then restoring yields: every other row restored byte-exact, a log line per failure, and a terminating error naming the unrestored count; an untampered restore completes cleanly with exit 0.

Title: Cross-implementation hash conformance
Requirement: Both restore implementations shall use identical canonical XXH128 (XXH3-128) content digests represented as 32 uppercase big-endian hexadecimal characters.
Rationale: Cross-platform deduplication, change detection and recovery require identical content identities.
AcceptanceCriteria: Digests agree across platforms for empty, one-byte, text, binary larger than 1 MiB, and Unicode-named inputs.

Title: Standalone Linux restore
Requirement: The standalone Linux restorer shall reproduce the source tree byte-for-byte using the backup folder and the declared commodity restore tools. The backup root shall restore the latest state; a dated snapshot shall restore its own indexed state without newer-state overlay. Missing stored locations shall recover from matching content in the shared pool; compressed content shall be expanded. The restorer shall refuse targets inside the backup, check capacity, and fail non-zero with the unrestored count when any entry cannot be restored.
Rationale: Linux recovery makes backups usable on a NAS or rescue host without the backup application.
AcceptanceCriteria: Windows-produced backups with compression on or off restore byte-exact on Linux from the live root and each snapshot; unrecoverable damage returns non-zero and names unrestored entries.

Title: Manifest portability across platforms
Requirement: The Linux restorer shall interpret the Windows-written index consistently: map RelativePath backslash separators to POSIX separators, parse LastWriteTimeStr as culture-independent ISO 8601 round-trip text, accept RFC 4180 quoted CSV fields including commas and quotes, and accept UTF-8 with an optional BOM and Unicode, bracketed and space-containing names.
Rationale: A cross-platform parsing divergence can silently corrupt recovery.
AcceptanceCriteria: Windows-written indexes including Unicode, bracketed and comma-containing names produce identical field values on Linux; separator mapping preserves every relative path.

Title: Linux backup interoperability
Requirement: A Linux backup producer shall use the shared nine-column index, one stored object per content hash and length, the current object-name contract, measured compression policy, dated supersession and shared-content preservation, so either restorer can recover what either producer wrote.
Rationale: Full parity lets Linux hosts run scheduled backups against the same targets (SN-023); interop is the anti-duplication guarantee that the contract, not the code, is the single source of truth.
AcceptanceCriteria: Backups produced on either platform restore byte-exact on Windows and Linux, with snapshot, deduplication and no-op behavior meeting SR-005 and SR-028.

Title: Linux container runtime
Requirement: The system shall provide a non-root Linux container runtime using portable JSON configuration and a writable source-state location distinct from a read-only source.
Rationale: The backup host can run the engine without installing its runtime and without modifying source files.
AcceptanceCriteria: The container reads a read-only source, persists its hash cache on the separate state location, creates a compressed backup with a complete restore kit, and supports byte-exact recovery.

Title: Run-state integrity gate
Requirement: When a populated backup index has missing or unparseable run state, the system shall refuse backup mutation with non-zero status rather than treating it as a first backup.
Rationale: Treating an existing backup as new can discard superseded history.
AcceptanceCriteria: If run state is removed or corrupted between runs while indexed entries remain, the next run fails non-zero, changes neither stored content nor the index, and creates no snapshot.

Title: Empty-source delete-all refusal
Requirement: When a previously populated source enumerates zero files, the system shall refuse the run before any backup mutation unless the set explicitly opts in with AllowEmptySource=true; an initially empty source remains valid.
Rationale: An unavailable or mis-mounted source can otherwise look like intentional deletion of everything.
AcceptanceCriteria: With prior manifest rows and an empty source, the run exits non-zero leaving backup bytes and manifest untouched; with AllowEmptySource=true the intentional delete-all proceeds and snapshots the prior state.

Title: Cross-platform tool discovery
Requirement: The system shall initialize and discover tools on non-Windows hosts without requiring Windows-only environment values. Compression tooling shall resolve through Tools.SevenZipPath or FILEBACKUP_7ZIP_PATH. FILEBACKUP_7Z_LEVEL shall accept one digit 0–9 and default to 9 when absent or empty. A malformed value shall not break initialization or restore; a Backup action with any CompressEnabled=true set shall instead refuse it before creating or mutating anything, naming the variable and allowed range, with status 2 under -ExitCode. Uncompressed-only runs and non-Backup actions shall be unaffected.
Rationale: Tool discovery must not make a non-Windows host unusable, and backup-only settings must not prevent recovery.
AcceptanceCriteria: Initialization succeeds without Windows environment paths. Compression tooling resolves through either supported override, and a missing-tool message names both. FILEBACKUP_7Z_LEVEL=10 does not break initialization or restore, but a compression-enabled backup exits 2 naming the variable and creates nothing; uncompressed-only and non-Backup operations remain usable.

Title: Index integrity evidence
Requirement: Every written backup index shall carry matching integrity evidence identifying its format version, entry count, byte length and XXH128 digest. This shall cover the live backup, staging, historical states, source cache and every index rewrite; each historical state shall have its own matching evidence. The index and its integrity evidence shall each be published atomically. Integrity evidence and incomplete publication artifacts shall be root-level infrastructure; nested user files with those names remain data.
Rationale: A truncated or replaced index can silently shrink the recovery job. A physical census cannot detect all such damage when content is shared; matching evidence must cover every written index.
AcceptanceCriteria: Every index has integrity evidence matching its own entry count, byte length and digest, including each snapshot's distinct index. Root-level evidence produces no orphan warning; a nested user file with the same name is backed up and restored.

Title: Restore verifies index integrity
Requirement: Before creating the target or restore log, both restorers shall validate the selected index's required schema columns and available integrity evidence. A byte-length or digest mismatch or unparseable evidence shall fail with code 3 before writing anything; count-only disagreement with matching length and digest shall warn and proceed. Missing evidence shall warn explicitly that the index is unverified and continue, except that -RequireWitness or --require-witness shall make absence fatal. Unknown evidence versions shall verify understood fields and warn, subject to the retired-format refusal in SR-061.
Rationale: Schema validation rejects unrelated text, while integrity verification catches damage that preserves the header. Missing evidence alone must not strand otherwise supported older backups.
AcceptanceCriteria: Truncated or edited index content fails with code 3; unrelated or unrecognizable index text fails with code 2, which takes precedence. Refusal creates neither target content nor log. Correctly regenerated evidence permits an intact supported index to restore; count-only disagreement warns and proceeds; absent evidence warns and permits byte-exact recovery unless strict mode is selected.

Title: Shared restore exit-code contract
Requirement: Both restorers shall use the same outcome table: 0 complete; 1 incomplete due to unrecoverable content; 2 usage or precondition failure; 3 index-integrity verification failure; 4 incomplete due to the host. Precedence shall be 2 > 3 > 4 > 1. Preconditions include bad arguments, missing or unrecognizable index, target inside backup, missing required tool and insufficient capacity. Recovery diagnostics shall distinguish missing content, unavailable dependency, unreadable storage and candidate errors, and the final summary shall count each class. In-process callers shall receive terminating errors; process entry points shall return the table's codes. A readable pool archive that cannot yield the expected payload shall be content damage (1) only after the host extraction capability has been shown usable; unreadable candidates or unusable extraction capability shall be host failures (4), with one cause per candidate. A row's own archive-shaped object that cannot be extracted shall remain host-class (4); bytes with no archive signature that reproduce neither valid form shall be ContentMismatch (1). ContentMismatch is content-class, while WriteMismatch from a verified source and readback failures are host-class.
Rationale: The backup host must distinguish bad invocation, damaged index, lost content and retriable host failures without parsing an undifferentiated error.
AcceptanceCriteria: The same failure returns the same documented code from both restorers; exit 0 requires every entry restored. An unopenable archive-shaped directly referenced object returns 4 with CandidateError; a non-archive replacement that matches no valid form returns 1 with ContentMismatch, while unaffected entries still restore. An unrelated invalid pool archive returns 1 on a host with usable extraction capability.

Title: Backup-side failure aggregation
Requirement: When preserving removed or superseded content, the system shall log each failed move as an ERROR naming the file and cause, continue processing other entries, and report overall failure with a summary count and non-zero exit.
Rationale: A single failed preservation must not hide other failures or prevent recoverable entries and historical state from being finalized.
AcceptanceCriteria: Two unmovable entries produce separate ERROR records and a summary count; movable entries are preserved, the snapshot is finalized, the run fails non-zero, no unfinished staging remains, and the next run can proceed.

Title: Versioned JSON configuration contract
Requirement: The JSON configuration shall be a versioned closed schema validated before dependency initialization or backup mutation. ConfigVersion shall be an integer-valued number, currently 2; version 1 and other unsupported versions shall be refused as unsupported, and missing or unparseable versions shall be refused. BackupSets shall contain at least one set; a single bare object shall also be accepted. Each set shall require non-empty string Name, SourcePath, BackupPath and ChangePath, HashRecalcFreq in A/E/D/W/M/Y/N case-insensitively, and boolean CompressEnabled. Optional values shall include SourceStatePath (default SourcePath), AllowEmptySource (boolean, default false), BrowseView (off|index, default off), ViewPath (default <BackupPath>_View), and CompressProbe (off|excluded-extensions|always, default always). BrowseView and CompressProbe shall use exact lowercase vocabulary. Optional Tools.SevenZipPath, Tools.FfprobePath and Secrets.ToEmail/FromEmail/SmtpServer shall be strings; Secrets.SmtpPort shall be integer-valued. All schema-defined strings and booleans shall retain their JSON types without coercion. Unknown keys, wrong types, missing required fields and Secrets.Credential shall fail naming the offending JSON path and expected type or values. Multiple JSON sets shall remain accepted with a warning naming their count and the IF-001 one-set convention. CLIXML shall remain an unversioned native-Windows form with the same per-set shape and value checks, exempt from the JSON version, closed-key and credential restrictions. PreserveFolderTree shall be refused by name in both formats. The published schema and runtime validation shall agree; an unchanged version-2 document omitting CompressProbe shall retain version 2 and resolve it to always. Invalid CompressProbe values, including mixed case, null and numbers, shall fail with status 2 and create nothing.
Rationale: Silent unknown-key handling and type coercion can change the operator's intent, particularly when a quoted false enables a destructive option. Configuration refusal must be explicit and distinguishable to the backup host.
AcceptanceCriteria: The shipped example is valid and, after path/tool retargeting, produces a byte-exact restorable backup. Missing, too-old, future or malformed versions; unknown top-level, set or tool keys; wrong string, boolean or integer types; invalid frequency; empty sets; and forbidden credentials are refused by their correct indexed key path before creating any artifact. Integral ConfigVersion 2.0 is accepted as 2. Omitted optional values resolve to their documented defaults; supported CLIXML remains usable. Invalid or mixed-case CompressProbe fails in both formats, while absence yields always. Published schema and runtime validation agree on accepted and refused configurations. Refusal neither creates a log directory nor truncates the prior global log.

Title: Configuration failure is distinguishable at the process boundary
Requirement: The backup entry point shall support -ExitCode: 0 for a complete run, 1 for failed backup sets, and 2 for an unreadable, missing, unsupported-format or invalid configuration. Without -ExitCode it shall retain terminating configuration errors and exit 1 for a failed set. The container entry point shall request the distinct status table. Configuration refusal shall create no artifacts and leave an existing global log intact.
Rationale: The backup host must distinguish a configuration that cannot succeed on retry from an operational backup failure.
AcceptanceCriteria: With -ExitCode, invalid, missing and unsupported configuration inputs return 2, set failures return 1 and success returns 0. Without it, in-process configuration failures still throw and failed sets retain exit 1. Configuration refusal preserves the old log and creates no new log directory or backup artifacts.

Title: Pruning preserves content needed by surviving states
Requirement: Removing a snapshot shall preserve every content hash-and-length key required by any surviving indexed state, including content whose sole copy is in the removed snapshot. Preserved content shall not be repacked or recompressed. No index entry shall be added, removed or reordered; RelativePath, Length, LastWriteTimeStr, xxH2Hash, Duplicate and MediaMBPerSec shall remain unchanged. Only planned storage-location and stored-form fields may change, with each rewritten index receiving its own matching integrity evidence. A removal that endangers no content shall copy none.
Rationale: Shared content can make an old snapshot hold the only copy needed by other states. Retention policy belongs to the backup host; safe removal and preservation belong to the backup system. Explicit surviving references prevent unreferenced copies and keep interrupted work checkable.
AcceptanceCriteria: Removing the oldest, middle, newest or sole snapshot leaves every surviving state and the latest state byte-exact restorable, with raw and compressed content. Preserved bytes match their indexed hash and length; index changes are confined to planned storage-location and form fields with identical entry sets and valid integrity evidence. Safe removals copy zero bytes; a quiescent store holds each content key once.

Title: Snapshot pruning is transactional and refuses loudly
Requirement: Snapshot removal shall preserve all surviving content throughout interruption and commit; before committing it shall establish that every surviving index entry resolves with the selected snapshot excluded. Explicit locations must exist with agreeing stored form; recovered content must agree with the row's form only for kits older than revision 2, whose behavior depends on that metadata. Refusals shall use precedence 2 > 3 > 4 > 1: invalid or missing integrity evidence is 3 (missing evidence may be overridden with -AllowUnverifiedIndex); invalid run state, busy staging, invalid or wildcard snapshot name, unreferenced target content, unresolved pool or incompatible older-kit form, insufficient measured destination capacity, and unavailable compression tooling for a compressed plan are 2; host I/O failures are 4 before commit. -DiscardUnreferencedData may override only the unreferenced-content refusal. Valid targets must be existing dated snapshots directly under the resolved change root. Capacity shall be assessed per destination volume, including UNC and POSIX paths, summing shared-volume demand and skipping unmeasurable volumes. Refused preflight shall leave the store unchanged, except completion of an already committed deletion for the same requested name. Interrupted operations shall be resumable by repeating the request without a separate recovery journal. Cleanup shall preserve user data even if its name resembles temporary residue, and run only after preflight and exclusive mutation access. -WhatIf shall report the classification and reclaim estimate without cleanup or mutation.
Rationale: Deletion must never make the surviving pool deficient. Distinct refusal classes let the backup host choose remediation or retry. Recomputing from stored state avoids a second recovery authority that could become stale.
AcceptanceCriteria: Interruption at each transaction boundary preserves surviving states and allows repeat invocation to finish. Preflight refusals preserve stored bytes and run state; overrides affect only their own refusal classes. Dry runs report the eventual reclaim figure and change nothing. Mixed-form stores with kits revision 2 or newer prune successfully; older incompatible kits cause a refusal naming the revision and -RefreshKits remedy. User content named like temporary residue survives refused, dry-run and successful operations. Refusal and dry run leave uncommitted residue untouched; undeletable committed residue reports 4.

Title: Snapshot inventory with dedup-aware reclaim figures
Requirement: The tool shall provide a read-only snapshot inventory with Name, Date, Rows, PhysicalBytes, BytesReclaimed and BytesReHomed. BytesReclaimed shall equal the whole-store space freed by removing that snapshot after preserving shared content, and BytesReHomed shall equal the copy cost. The inventory shall be returned as objects in-process and one JSON document at the process boundary.
Rationale: Because of dedup a snapshot folder's size is NOT what deleting it frees, so a wrapper deciding what to keep cannot compute the number itself; and IF-001 requires the retention decision to be made outside FileBackup while the arithmetic stays inside it.
AcceptanceCriteria: The reported BytesReclaimed for each snapshot equals the measured whole-store size drop after actually removing it, and BytesReHomed equals the measured bytes copied; running the report leaves every file in the store byte-identical; the JSON parses to one object per snapshot carrying all six fields.

Title: Retention is invocable at the container boundary
Requirement: The backup interface shall accept -Action Backup|Prune|Snapshots (default Backup) and -Snapshot <name[,...]> for one configured set, support -WhatIf for removal, and emit inventory as JSON on stdout. Under -ExitCode it shall report 0 pruned, 1 batch incomplete without data loss, 2 usage/precondition, 3 index verification failure, or 4 retriable host I/O, with precedence 2 > 3 > 4 > 1. The container interface shall accept FILEBACKUP_ACTION (default backup) or a leading backup, prune or snapshots word, map FILEBACKUP_SNAPSHOT and FILEBACKUP_DRY_RUN to the corresponding selection and dry-run behavior, and preserve flag-only invocations. The standalone POSIX restore capability shall not offer pruning, and no restore shall require pruning.
Rationale: The backup host needs one-shot retention operations with the same outcome vocabulary as backup and restore, while existing container invocations retain their behavior.
AcceptanceCriteria: The container snapshots action emits parseable JSON and exits 0 without mutation; valid pruning exits 0 with every surviving state restorable; an unknown name exits 2 without mutation; a dry run exits 0 without mutation. Default and flag-only invocation behavior is preserved, and standalone POSIX restoration offers no removal operation.

Title: Storage-form verification and repair
Requirement: The system shall offer an opt-in Verify action, separate from normal backup, comparing every index entry in the live backup and snapshots with stored bytes. Explicit stored locations must exist and their extension, Compressed value and physical form must agree; entries recovered from the pool shall be checked against the located form. Verification shall change nothing and report each finding's entry, folder and class. Explicit repair shall fix only unambiguous form findings grounded in bytes in the entry's own folder, keeping content unchanged and updating all entries sharing the same object together. Repair shall preserve all six logical columns and refresh each changed index's own integrity evidence. Findings on entries without an explicit location shall remain report-only. Outcomes shall use SR-040.
Rationale: Incorrect metadata can validate itself indefinitely if never compared with bytes. An opt-in audit exposes those discrepancies without adding a full physical check to every ordinary backup.
AcceptanceCriteria: Wrong form flags, misleading archive names and missing explicit locations each produce a finding and non-zero status with no mutation. Repair corrects unambiguous cases, including every entry sharing an object, and subsequent verification and restore succeed without dangling references. Clean stores with raw or compressed content exit 0; ordinary backup does not invoke the opt-in audit, and an unchanged backup after repair is idempotent.

Title: Restore resolves storage form from the located file
Requirement: When an entry is recovered from the shared content pool, both restorers shall use the located content's proven physical form rather than the entry's Compressed value to decide whether to expand it. A candidate whose expanded payload does not match, including one that fails to expand, shall also be considered as raw source bytes before rejection. Outcomes shall follow SR-040.
Rationale: An entry's form metadata may describe another copy at another time. Mixed raw and compressed storage is legitimate, so a located object must be interpreted from its own content; an original archive can itself be the bytes to recover.
AcceptanceCriteria: After a compression-policy change, an entry recoverable only from an opposite-form copy restores byte-exact with exit 0 through both restorers in either direction. Genuine original archive content also restores byte-exact. Unrecoverable content returns 1 and host failures return 4.

Title: No run deletes a data file a live row still claims
Requirement: No step of a backup run shall delete or move out of the pool a data file that any row of the final manifest still references, and rows that share one physical data file shall be treated as one unit, so no operation can leave a row pointing at a path that is gone.
Rationale: Shared content must remain available to every final live entry, including frozen entries and entries whose replacement failed; testing survival only against the source walk would miss those dependencies.
AcceptanceCriteria: Removing either member of a dedup group leaves the survivors' object in the pool and every state restorable byte-exact with exit 0; a superseded object still claimed by a frozen row, or by a row whose replacement copy failed, is retained rather than parked; no data file referenced by the final manifest is missing after any run.

Title: Backup-side capacity preflight
Requirement: Before writing any backup or staging bytes, the system shall estimate the new deduplicated content by uncompressed length and the superseded or removed content that must be copied across volumes. It shall sum demands sharing a volume and refuse a set before mutation when measured free space is insufficient, naming the volume, required bytes and free bytes. Backup and restore capacity checks shall work on Windows and Linux using actual volume identities, treating a mount and paths beneath it as one volume.
Rationale: Filling a destination midway through a run can leave the index and content out of step. Capacity checks must work for mounted Linux storage as well as Windows volumes.
AcceptanceCriteria: A set whose new content exceeds destination capacity refuses before creating or modifying files, leaves the tree byte-identical, names the volume and required/free bytes and returns non-zero. Missing-content entries being healed contribute their length to demand. A fitting set proceeds; combined demands exceeding one shared volume refuse even if each fits separately. Capacity measurements work for Windows drive paths and rooted POSIX paths, identify a mount and its subdirectories as one volume, and the restore capacity refusal works on Linux.

Title: Backup heals missing stored content
Requirement: When a live index entry lacks stored content but its source path remains, the next backup shall restore its recoverability by copying source content or reusing a surviving copy. Such an entry shall never be adopted as existing content for a new file until real bytes are available. Healing that changes the index shall preserve the superseded indexed state as for any other changed run.
Rationale: External deletion must not cause indefinite silent success over missing content or propagate missing-content entries to newly encountered duplicates.
AcceptanceCriteria: After external deletion, matching available source or pool content lets the next run exit 0 with all entries recoverable byte-exact. A new matching file never inherits missing bytes. A missing-content entry is healed even if source metadata is unchanged; runs with no such damage retain their behavior.

Title: Verification reports rows whose bytes are gone from the pool
Requirement: Verify shall report every index entry whose content is absent from the entire pool as PoolUnresolvable in its JSON findings with exit 1. This pool check shall always include the live backup and every snapshot regardless of -BackupRootOnly. -RepairStorage shall leave lost-content findings report-only; recovery requires available source content on a later backup or restoration of content into the pool.
Rationale: Verification must expose unrestorable content even when the owner never invokes pruning.
AcceptanceCriteria: Content absent everywhere yields PoolUnresolvable naming the folder and RelativePath with exit 1. A missing explicit location whose content survives elsewhere yields PoolDataPathMissing instead, since restore can recover it and backup can heal it. A clean pool yields an empty findings document and exit 0; -RepairStorage does not claim to repair absent bytes.

Title: Non-portable filenames are refused loudly at backup time
Requirement: Before opening or hashing a source file, the system shall reject a path component invalid on either Windows or Linux: Windows-forbidden characters (< > : " | ? * and controls including newlines), trailing dot or space, reserved device stems CON, PRN, AUX, NUL, COM1–COM9 or LPT1–LPT9 regardless of case or extension, and on non-Windows hosts a literal backslash. Each skipped file shall produce one ERROR naming the file and reason, fail the set non-zero and allow other files to continue. No new entry shall be written for unstored content; an existing entry at the still-present invalid name shall remain frozen with its stored bytes.
Rationale: Portable names are necessary for interchangeable restores. Clear refusal lets the owner correct names at the source rather than producing content that only one platform can recover. Generated stored names are independently constrained by SR-069.
AcceptanceCriteria: Each forbidden component class is refused with a named reason; Unicode, brackets, parentheses and ordinary spaces remain accepted. A hostable trailing-dot name causes one skipping ERROR and exit 1, while other files are backed up and any prior entry at that name and its bytes remain intact.

Title: Restore verifies the bytes it wrote
Requirement: After writing any restored entry, both restorers shall verify its length and content digest against the index. A mismatch shall remove the bad output and trigger at most one recovery from another pool copy when the source was not already proven. Unverifiable content shall be counted unrestored as ContentMismatch, exit 1, never success. A mismatch after writing a source already proven correct shall instead be WriteMismatch, a host failure with exit 4; unreadable verification output shall likewise be host-class and shall be retained.
Rationale: Resolvable stored paths can still contain wrong, altered or truncated payloads; successful recovery requires verification of what was actually written.
AcceptanceCriteria: A data file altered to wrong-payload, same-length-bitflip or truncated content restores byte-exact from a surviving pool copy (exit 0, one WARN logged naming the row) when a good copy exists; the row is named in the SR-029 unrestored accounting as ContentMismatch (exit 1) when no good copy exists; an untampered restore is unaffected.

Title: Hidden and dot-prefixed files are captured and located
Requirement: Source capture, content recovery, snapshot discovery, pruning cleanup and byte accounting shall include hidden, system and dot-prefixed files and directories. Exclusion shall be by SourcePath scope; no per-set hidden-file exclusion setting shall be introduced. This requirement shall not alter symbolic-link traversal semantics. Only the Windows volume-root pseudo-folders specified in SR-074 are exempt.
Rationale: Visibility attributes must not silently remove source content or make recoverable stored content invisible.
AcceptanceCriteria: Dot files, nested dot directories and Windows Hidden or System files and directories are indexed and restore byte-exact with compression on or off. Hidden and dot-named pool content remains discoverable, and no new exclusion configuration key exists.

Title: Content addressing is the only storage layout
Requirement: The system shall use one content-addressed storage layout conforming to SR-069; no configuration shall select a mirrored path-addressed layout.
Rationale: Distinct content must not overwrite another saved object through reuse of a logical path.
AcceptanceCriteria: Every nonblank stored location in the index conforms to the current object-name contract and StoredAsHashSize is 'Hash'; no configuration selects another layout.

Title: Stored objects are immutable and name-proven
Requirement: The system shall preserve the bytes of every stored object still claimed by a live index entry, and any newly stored object's content identity shall agree with the bytes it holds.
Rationale: Shared references promise particular bytes; overwriting an object would invalidate every saved path that still depends on it.
AcceptanceCriteria: Editing one of two identical files never changes an object still claimed by an index entry; the earlier snapshot restores the old content at every shared path.

Title: Dedup covers content first seen within one run
Requirement: Content with the same (xxH2Hash,Length) appearing several times in a single run shall be stored once, with every logical name referencing that one physical object.
Rationale: Deduplication must cover newly encountered duplicates within the same run, not only content from earlier runs.
AcceptanceCriteria: Identical files first seen together yield exactly one physical pool object and one shared stored location.

Title: A legacy-form store is refused, not converted or restored
Requirement: The system shall not change the physical form of existing stored content when CompressEnabled changes; only new content follows the new policy. Backup shall refuse retired formats before mutation with a fresh-BackupPath remedy, while Verify shall report them as findings. Both restorers shall refuse retired formats with exit 2 before target writes. Retired format evidence includes StoredAsHashSize=Original, an integrity-format version below the supported version, a stored location containing a path separator, or the retired base-85 name shape with a separator space at position 16. A merely damaged location that matches neither current nor retired grammar shall remain eligible for per-entry audit, healing and recovery rather than causing whole-store format refusal.
Rationale: Repacking an existing store risks working content and is unnecessary for per-file compression. Positive retired-format identification distinguishes unsupported stores from repairable damaged entries. Format evidence and name shape complement each other: missing evidence and blank locations cannot classify format, but recovery by content can still succeed.
AcceptanceCriteria: Changing CompressEnabled leaves existing objects untouched; new content follows the setting and a mixed-form store restores byte-exact and audits clean. Legacy Original and retired base-85 stores are refused by backup without mutation and by both restorers with exit 2 and no target writes; Verify reports a finding. Retired names are recognized even without integrity evidence. Merely damaged locations still audit, heal and recover. A store with retired object names, all locations blank and no integrity evidence remains byte-exact recoverable by content.

Title: Generated browse view
Requirement: When BrowseView=index, the system shall provide a tab-separated browse index, per-folder HTML pages and a root search page outside the source and backup roots, covering every logical path including duplicate siblings. It shall refresh when the indexed logical rows change and on Action View. Backup correctness, verification, pruning and restoration shall not depend on the browse view.
Rationale: A complete path-based view makes shared content discoverable; per-folder pages keep very large libraries practical to browse.
AcceptanceCriteria: The view's entries equal the indexed RelativePath set, with an archive suffix when the entry is marked compressed. Changed logical rows trigger rebuilding; Action View is idempotent; verification, pruning accounting and both restorers ignore the view.

Title: Configuration contract v2
Requirement: The JSON contract shall use ConfigVersion 2 and refuse PreserveFolderTree by name in every configuration format. BrowseView shall accept off|index, reserving and refusing link. ViewPath shall be on the backup volume and shall not overlap BackupPath, ChangePath, SourcePath or SourceStatePath in either direction, including equality. A view root containing nongenerated content shall not be erased. CompressProbe shall accept exact-lowercase off|excluded-extensions|always in both configuration formats, defaulting to always. An optional key with a default may be added to version 2 only if unchanged documents retain their meaning; older closed-schema implementations may reject it by name. Required, removed, retyped or meaning-changing keys shall require a version change.
Rationale: An obsolete configuration must be refused rather than silently reinterpreted. Because CLIXML is not closed-schema, removed keys require explicit refusal there too.
AcceptanceCriteria: PreserveFolderTree fails with status 2 naming the key in JSON and CLIXML. Invalid BrowseView, off-volume or overlapping ViewPath, and a view root holding user content are refused without deletion. Invalid or mixed-case CompressProbe fails by name in both formats; an unchanged version-2 document without it loads with always.

Title: Store audits scale linearly
Requirement: The unreferenced-data-file audit shall be linear in manifest rows plus on-disk data files.
Rationale: The ordinary backup audit must remain practical for libraries containing hundreds of thousands of files; repeatedly searching all index entries for every stored file does not scale.
AcceptanceCriteria: With 10,000 index entries and 10,000 pool files, the audit completes within its declared time budget and reports missing and unreferenced data. A stored location that names root-level infrastructure is cleared rather than treated as user content.

Title: Empty directories and folder attributes are recorded and restored
Requirement: Each saved state shall retain advisory metadata for source directories containing no file anywhere beneath them or carrying Hidden, System, ReadOnly or NotContentIndexed. Both restorers shall recreate those directories and apply supported Windows attributes after file content is written and verified. Absent, unreadable or malformed directory metadata shall not fail restoration or change the prior file-only behavior; it shall not participate in index-integrity verification. Unenumerable directories shall not be recorded. POSIX recovery shall create directories and report attributes it cannot apply.
Rationale: A file-only index omits empty folders and directory attributes. ReadOnly matters even without directory write-protection semantics because it affects customized folder views.
AcceptanceCriteria: Empty and nested-empty directories and a Hidden+System folder are recorded and recreated, with supported attributes restored. A tree without empty or attributed directories adds no directory metadata. Missing or garbage metadata still permits successful file recovery; POSIX recovery reports unapplied attributes. Each snapshot retains the directory metadata of its own state.

Title: Restored files carry their own modification time
Requirement: Both restorers shall apply each restored file's own LastWriteTimeStr from the manifest row it was restored from, after that file has passed its post-write (Length, xxH2Hash) verification. A blank or unparseable value shall be logged and the row shall still count as restored; the timestamp shall never fail a restore.
Rationale: Shared stored content must not force all recovered paths to inherit one owner's timestamp. Each indexed path has its own recorded time; file attributes remain outside this contract.
AcceptanceCriteria: Identical files with different times recover their own times under both restorers with compression on or off, as does unique content. A blank or invalid LastWriteTimeStr warns but preserves successful byte recovery and exit 0.

Title: A transiently unreadable source file is retried, not lost
Requirement: A copy or compress that fails for a reason which could change shall be retried after a short delay, up to three attempts per file, bounded by a per-run retry budget shared across the whole set; a failure that cannot change on a retry shall not consume the budget. A file still unreadable when its attempts are exhausted shall be logged as an error naming the attempt count, shall receive NO manifest row for the content that was not stored, and shall mark the set failed. A file that already had a manifest row from an earlier run shall keep that row, which names bytes the store still holds.
Rationale: A unique file can suffer a momentary lock without an alternate readable duplicate. Retrying transient failure preserves the source scan's obligation, while a shared budget prevents systemic errors from turning an unattended run into hours of waiting.
AcceptanceCriteria: A transiently locked file becomes backed up when its lock clears after the first attempt, with a visible retry. A new permanently unreadable file exhausts three attempts while budget remains, fails the set and gets no entry for unstored content; a prior stored entry survives. A directory at the destination fails immediately without consuming retry budget. A spent budget stops further waiting, reports exhaustion and fails remaining unreadable files.

Title: Restore uses actual stored form
Requirement: Both restorers shall recover raw or archived content based on the stored bytes, whether directly located or recovered from the pool. They shall preserve a source archive stored raw as the original bytes rather than expanding it. Compressed shall remain in the schema and may inform the approximate capacity estimate, but shall not decide correctness.
Rationale: Stored metadata can disagree with bytes, and a source file can itself be an archive regardless of its name. Recovery must distinguish stored packaging from original archive content using evidence in the bytes.
AcceptanceCriteria: Both restorers recover byte-exact with every Compressed value flipped, for raw, tool-compressed and original-archive content. Original archives stored raw are never expanded; an object matching neither form fails loudly as content damage.

Title: Stored-object name grammar
Requirement: Stored object names shall follow "<hash>_<len><ext>": the complete 128-bit content digest encoded in 22 left-padded base-57 characters, an underscore, the unpadded base-57 content length, and the opaque extension specified by SR-070. The alphabet shall be the 62 alphanumerics excluding 0, O, I, l and 1, with '2' as zero. Overwide fixed-width values shall be refused without truncation, and decoded hash values of 2^128 or more shall be refused. The extension shall not be parsed as part of the encoded identity.
Rationale: The name must preserve the complete digest while avoiding leading punctuation, separator spaces and shell metacharacters in its encoded fields. Unpadded lengths avoid unnecessary zero digits. Twenty-two base-57 characters hold 128 bits; on case-insensitive volumes the folded alphabet provides about 111.92 bits of name distinction.
AcceptanceCriteria: Names have a 22-character base-57 hash field, underscore, nonempty base-57 length field and opaque extension. All 32 hexadecimal digest digits roundtrip, including leading-zero and high-bit values; zero length uses the single zero glyph. Overwide encoding and decoding to 2^128 or more are rejected; retired base-85 names do not parse.

Title: A stored object carries its source extension, opaquely
Requirement: The extension of a stored object's name shall be the elected owner's source extension verbatim, or '.7z' when this tool compressed it, and shall be treated as OPAQUE: it shall not be constrained to SR-069's alphabet, and it MAY BE EMPTY. A source file with no extension shall be stored and restored like any other. No guard shall classify a store by the characters in an object's extension.
Rationale: Valid source extensions can contain spaces, underscores, brackets or non-ASCII characters, and valid files can have no extension. Those cases must not be mistaken for legacy format or rejected during storage.
AcceptanceCriteria: An extensionless file restores byte-exact through both restorers with compression on or off. Files with spaces, underscores, brackets or non-ASCII in their extension remain storable, parseable and restorable and are not classified as legacy.

Title: POSIX restore portability beyond GNU
Requirement: The POSIX restorer shall work identically on GNU and BSD userlands meeting the declared floor of bash 4+, a compatible GNU awk capability, XXH128 command-line hashing and archive extraction when compressed content exists. File sizes, temporary storage, timestamps, free space, snapshot enumeration and canonical paths shall behave consistently. An unmet tool floor or unresolvable canonical path shall fail with precondition code 2 and remediation, never falsely report content, index-integrity or host damage against an intact backup.
Rationale: Passing a dependency check is insufficient if platform-specific tool behavior then produces false integrity failures or bypasses target containment. An intact backup must not be reported damaged because standard userlands differ.
AcceptanceCriteria: On a userland with BSD coreutils and the declared floor installed, a store restores byte-exact from the backup root and from any snapshot; a manifest with a valid witness verifies; the data pool contains every sibling snapshot; compressed rows expand; each restored file carries its own mtime. A target path that cannot be canonicalised exits 2 naming the reason, and a '..' component is refused rather than reduced.

Title: Double-click restore entry points
Requirement: Every backup root and dated snapshot shall include double-click restore entry points for Windows and macOS. A no-argument interactive launch shall start target selection and preserve the displayed result; scripted launches shall return the SR-040 status unchanged and shall not hold the window.
Rationale: Recovery should not require recalling command parameters. Interactive result visibility must not block automated callers.
AcceptanceCriteria: A no-argument desktop launch offers a folder picker, restores and holds the result showing its exit code. Argument-bearing launches return the status without prompts or pauses, including command-shell and batch callers. macOS starts from the kit's own location; double-click is supported only on volumes preserving or synthesizing executability, including FAT/exFAT/NTFS. Elsewhere the documented explicit --pick-target shell invocation needs no executable bit.

Title: Graphical target selection, never in automation
Requirement: When a restore starts without a target in an interactive desktop session, it shall offer a native folder picker; with a console but no desktop it shall offer a typed prompt; with neither it shall print usage and exit 2. The POSIX restorer shall require explicit --pick-target for selection; missing --target-root alone shall remain usage plus exit 2.
Rationale: Target selection improves access, but a dialog must not introduce blocking into automation or change an existing missing-target failure into an implicit interactive action.
AcceptanceCriteria: -NonInteractive, redirected input and sessions with neither console nor desktop yield usage and exit 2 without prompting. -NoGui or FILEBACKUP_NO_GUI=1 uses the typed-prompt path where interaction is permitted. A cancelled or unavailable picker falls back to a typed prompt on Windows or usage plus exit 2 on POSIX, never to a default target. Explicit --pick-target restores into the chosen folder.

Title: Volume-root pseudo-folders are not data
Requirement: Source capture and restore pool discovery shall exclude the Windows volume-metadata and recycle-bin pseudo-directories and their descendants only when directly under a genuine drive or UNC-share volume root, case-insensitively. Their presence shall neither fail a backup set, contribute indexed files nor cause a pool read failure. Identically named directories nested in the tree or directly under an ordinary directory shall remain user data.
Rationale: System-managed volume metadata and discarded files are not the owner's source data. Attempting to enumerate them can create false backup failures or misclassify genuinely missing content as a retriable host problem; excluding similarly named ordinary folders would instead lose real data.
AcceptanceCriteria: A volume-root backup succeeds with no entries beneath either system pseudo-directory, while nested same-name directories are preserved. At an ordinary root, both same-name directories are captured fully. An unreadable system pseudo-directory does not turn missing pool content from ContentMissing/1 into StorageUnreadable/4. Matching is case-insensitive.
Permutations: root=set{volume,ordinary}; location=set{root,nested}; folder=set{System Volume Information,$RECYCLE.BIN}; side=set{backup,restore}

Title: Staging ownership and safe abandoned-run recovery
Requirement: A backup shall establish exclusive staging ownership before using staging, keep its liveness observable throughout long blocking work, and abort without cleanup if ownership is lost. Diagnostic identity shall include the set, host, container, boot, process and start time; process identity alone shall not prove liveness across hosts or containers. Liveness updates shall occur every 60 seconds, verify the initial update synchronously, report later failures, never refresh a successor's ownership, and cease completely when stopped. A stale owner shall be declared dead only after its declared timeout, with a minimum of 1800 seconds, and unchanged liveness over a confirmation interval of max(90 seconds, declared heartbeat interval + 30 seconds), with the positive declared interval capped at 600 seconds. Unparseable records shall use the 1800-second and 90-second floors; unreadable evidence shall refuse. Future-dated evidence shall count as fresh. Fresh empty staging, live or changing ownership, prune ownership of any age, content-bearing staging, symbolic links and indeterminate access shall refuse; only stale empty or confirmed stale backup-marker-only staging may be reclaimed, subject to SR-083's incomplete-index exception. Recovery shall preserve unexpected content, recheck ownership after claiming abandoned staging, and retain it with guidance when safe cleanup or reversal fails. Concurrent reclaimers shall leave one owner; a former owner shall not alter or delete its successor's work. Ownership shall be checked before staging the prior index, preserving removed content, preserving superseded content, publishing the live index and finalizing the snapshot. Unreadable ownership evidence shall be retried up to three times about 300 ms apart; a changed identity shall abort immediately without cleanup. Final snapshots shall contain no active ownership record. Each branch shall log its distinct [SR-075/reclaimed], [SR-075/owner-live], [SR-075/content-refused], [SR-075/prune-held], [SR-075/lock-lost] or [SR-075/lock-held] token without adding exit codes. Exclusive mutation protection shall cover finalization even after marker removal; failure to acquire it shall refuse, while successful acquisition shall never substitute for abandoned-staging checks.
Rationale: An interrupted run should not permanently block future backups, but an incorrect reclaim can destroy the only copy of saved content. Container process identities and clock offsets cannot establish safe ownership alone. Confirmed liveness, ownership checks and fail-closed cleanup protect against delayed or resumed writers, metadata caching and unexpected content. Longer stale thresholds delay recovery; shorter ones risk a live run. Distinct log outcomes let the backup host apply its own alarm policy.
AcceptanceCriteria: A confirmed stale marker-only abandoned run is reclaimed with the reclaimed token and the next run completes; a live run is refused with owner identity, start time and last-liveness age and no store mutation. Liveness advances during a long blocking hash and update failures are reported. Content-bearing, prune-held, unreadable, linked or indeterminate staging remains untouched. Torn or unknown-schema records can recover only under the stated age and confirmation floors. Racing reclaimers leave one owner; a displaced owner aborts without touching successor state. Content appearing during recovery is preserved and guidance is shown. Changed ownership at any of the five protected boundaries aborts before that phase mutates the pool. A live owner with a slow clock is still refused. Final snapshots contain no active ownership metadata and prune without spurious unreferenced-content refusals. These outcomes hold on exFAT under Windows and Linux containers.

Title: Measured compression decision
Requirement: For newly written content with CompressEnabled=true, the system shall apply CompressProbe modes off|excluded-extensions|always, exact lowercase, default always. Disabled compression shall store raw without probing or resolving compression tooling. Mode off shall use the extension policy. Files below 256 KiB shall use that policy without probing in every mode; excluded-extensions shall exempt listed types. Otherwise a measured aggregate saving of at least 0.10 shall select compression, with no filename override. Missing measurements shall fall back to the extension policy with one WARN per written content group and shall not fail the run. Sampling shall not modify source or destination content, shall reject observed changes in source length or modification time, and shall cost no more than 3 × 256 KiB per newly written group. A readable duplicate shall serve measurement when the owner is locked; existing-content reuse and in-run twins shall not incur probes, and retrying group members shall not repeat the measurement. Each written group shall log one DEBUG compress-decision with reason and aggregate/window ratios, using Reason values CompressDisabled, ModeOff, BelowFloor, ListExempt, ProbeUnavailable, ProbeCompressible and ProbeIncompressible. Set summaries shall report Probe stored raw object/byte counts, Probe compressed object count and Probe reads byte count, with stored counts reflecting successful writes. Existing content shall not be re-formed; restore semantics, exit codes and ConfigVersion 2 shall remain unchanged. Stored extension and Compressed metadata shall agree with the actual decision.
Rationale: Extensions alone cannot reveal compressibility, and a small compressible head must not send an otherwise incompressible large file through expensive compression. Aggregate measurement bounds that cost. Fallback preserves availability when sampling cannot run; shared group decisions bound reads and warnings. Sampling is deterministic within a host and run, though near-threshold results may vary across runtime versions; either stored form must remain byte-exact recoverable.
AcceptanceCriteria: With compression disabled, every mode and extension class stores raw and performs no probe. Above 256 KiB under always, random bytes remain raw, text compresses, a random file with a 64 KiB text head remains raw, and one-third-text content compresses; listed archive or image extensions do not override measurements. Under off, the extension policy applies; excluded-extensions preserves exemptions and probes other eligible content; below the floor all modes use the extension policy. Files smaller than three sample windows use one full-file sample. Unreadable or vanished paths yield no measurement; a group with no readable member falls back with exactly one WARN without failing merely because of the probe. Random samples have aggregate ratio at least 0.98. Reused content and twins incur zero probe reads; retried groups probe once and warn at most once; a readable twin avoids ProbeUnavailable. Logs and summary counts match measured read cost and successfully stored objects, including reported container read bytes and elapsed cost. Invalid mode values fail with status 2 and no artifacts in JSON and CLIXML; absent mode resolves to always. Mixed-form output verifies clean and restores byte-exact through both restorers.

Title: Atomic manifest publish
Requirement: Every published backup index shall remain either the complete previous version or the complete new version throughout writing and after interruption, never a torn or truncated version. Abandoned incomplete publication data shall not be read or appended to and shall be replaced from scratch on the next write. An ordinary publication failure shall preserve the prior destination and clean up incomplete publication data.
Rationale: A torn rewrite can destroy the only index of a historical state. Complete publication is necessary for safe recovery after a killed run, even when interrupted integrity-evidence publication causes a loud refusal.
AcceptanceCriteria: Interruption before, during or after preparation or publication leaves the index equal to the complete old or new version, including when incomplete prepared data is empty or half-written. Interruption after publishing the index but before matching integrity evidence fails verification loudly. The next successful write consumes leftover incomplete data and publishes a complete new index.

Title: Incomplete index publication data is infrastructure
Requirement: Incomplete index-publication artifacts at the live backup or snapshot root shall be infrastructure, never source data, orphan warnings or storage-form findings; identically named nested user files shall remain data. Abandoned-staging classification shall recognize the exact case-sensitive incomplete-index artifact as noncontent and remove it during safe reclaim or owned-staging cleanup. Other content, including a completed staged index, shall continue to prevent abandoned-staging reclaim.
Rationale: Incomplete publication data is not a unique saved copy, so it must not permanently wedge a dead run or pollute later audits. Its narrow recognition must not excuse real content.
AcceptanceCriteria: A root-level incomplete-index artifact yields no warnings, audit findings or indexed entry across three backups and is consumed by the next write. A nested same-name file is preserved. Stale marker-only staging plus that artifact is reclaimable; fresh staging remains live; added data or a complete staged index refuses without byte changes. Early failure cleans such artifacts only from owned staging.

Title: Atomic manifest publish needs no kit refresh
Requirement: Changing index publication to preserve complete versions shall not require refreshing existing restore kits or change restoration of supported stores.
Rationale: A change confined to writing the index provides no reason to rewrite historical recovery kits when their reading contract remains compatible.
AcceptanceCriteria: A supported store written with atomic index publication remains identically restorable by its existing compatible kit without Verify -RefreshKits.

Title: Exclusive store mutation through finalization
Requirement: Backup, pruning, storage-form repair and kit refresh shall exclude concurrent participating store mutations for their whole operation, including direct API calls, state-dependent reads and snapshot finalization after active ownership metadata is removed. Backup shall obtain exclusion before reading prior state or integrity gates and shall not truncate the set log before those gates; acquisition refusal shall append one line to the live holder's log. Pruning shall obtain exclusion before even completing previously committed deletion and retain it for the batch. Exclusion shall end after the operation or on failure and shall be released when its process dies. Dry-run mutation operations, read-only Verify, Snapshots, View and restores shall not obtain mutation exclusion. Windows exclusion shall apply among openers and SMB clients; Linux/macOS exclusion is limited to cooperating processes on the same kernel, including containers sharing storage, when the filesystem and runtime support locking. Cross-host SMB/NFS or mixed local/server access is not guaranteed there; older-owner liveness and confirmation safeguards remain required wherever exclusion is ineffective.
Rationale: Finalization can temporarily lack ownership metadata while staging holds unique saved bytes. Exclusive mutation must also cover subsequent state updates and historical deduplication; otherwise another run can act on incomplete state or mutate history concurrently. Automatic process-death release distinguishes a dead holder from a live one.
AcceptanceCriteria: On Windows with PowerShell 7, competing backup, prune, repair and kit refresh operations are refused with lock-held throughout finalization and after snapshot publication while the holder still works. Stored content and indexes remain unchanged, aside from the specified refusal-log append. Repair and refresh report code 2 through Verify; read-only Verify remains usable. Exclusion is released after success, ordinary failure, staging refusal, ownership loss and process termination.

Title: Conservative mutation-exclusion failure handling
Requirement: Any inability to obtain mutation exclusion, including contention, access denial, transient external access, an invalid lock location or I/O failure, shall be treated as a live holder. After at most three attempts about 250 ms apart, the caller shall log [SR-075/lock-held] and refuse without creating, classifying, moving or deleting staging, data or indexes. Backup shall fail its set; named prune requests shall report Refused, staging-busy, code 2; repair and refresh shall throw and Verify shall report 2. A repair without a change root shall refuse likewise; a nonexistent change root shall be created before exclusion is obtained. Obtaining exclusion shall never prove that an older staging owner is dead or override any SR-017/SR-075 refusal.
Rationale: A false live-holder classification costs a refused run, while a false free-holder classification can destroy unique content. Older participants may not use the exclusion facility; brief retries absorb transient external access without weakening refusal rules.
AcceptanceCriteria: Free exclusion with fresh older-owner evidence still yields owner-live; free exclusion with stale evidence plus content still yields content-refused. A held exclusion refuses even otherwise reclaimable staging without changes; after release the same abandoned staging can be reclaimed. Invalid lock locations, I/O failures and access denial cause backup and prune refusal with stored bytes unchanged.

Title: Persistent mutation-exclusion infrastructure
Requirement: Mutation-exclusion infrastructure shall remain usable when marked read-only and shall not be interpreted as user data, a snapshot or historical change content by any backup, audit, inventory, pruning or restore operation. Adding it shall not require refreshing existing restore kits.
Rationale: Removing and recreating filesystem lock identity can let simultaneous processes hold different locks for the same store. Persistent empty infrastructure avoids that race and must remain invisible to content consumers.
AcceptanceCriteria: After three runs the exclusion artifact remains empty; while held it does not change snapshot inventory, audit findings or byte-exact recovery of the latest and historical states. A read-only attribute does not prevent acquisition; Windows prevents deletion while held. Existing kits remain usable without refresh.
